newsitem.title: USA: NYS comptroller weighs running for Gov - paper.
newsitem.headline: NYS comptroller weighs running for Gov - paper.

text.p: New York State Comptroller H. Carl McCall said he would announce in November whether he would challenge Gov. George Pataki for governor, the Albany Times Union reported Wednesday.
The potential Democrat challenger, the state's top African-American elected official, was quoted as saying: "All across the state, people are encouraging me to do so. Obviously, we're looking at it."
He added, "It's a good possibility, but there are two or three things I have to look at. The most difficult thing is money."
McCall said he did not know if he had the "desire or ability" to raise $15 million to run a strong campaign against Pataki, a Republican, the paper said.

In an effort to pressure his rival, McCall said he no longer would accept fees for giving speeches. The two men acknowledged last month that they had accepted speaking fees, a practice that raises questions about conflicts of interest, the Times Union said.

Pataki made more than $60,000 in the last year for four speeches made to private, out-of-state groups, while McCall said he got $2,500 last November for a speech given in New York City to the Minority Interchange, a New Jersey-based group of black and Hispanic professionals.
The governor has defended the practice, saying he saw no reason to stop giving speeches and nothing improper in addressing out-of-state groups on his own time, the paper said.
A spokesman for Pataki told the Times Union, "He has already answered all the question on that. Go back and read the (newspaper) clips."

The paper added there was speculation Pataki in part was motivated by heavy debt. The New York Times said last week that the governor was carrying mortgages totaling nearly $1 million on four properties. About 40 percent of the Pataki family income goes toward mortgage costs and property taxes.
